messages.content: Write an engineering team's year in review post for an internal blog. Around 250 words.

**Draft — 2026 in review** (swap the placeholder numbers and names for your real ones)

---

### The year, briefly

A deploy in January cost us 41 minutes. It now costs six. That goes first because nearly everything below got easier once we stopped sitting on our hands waiting for a pipeline.

Splitting the monolith ran three quarters instead of two. Nobody's fault. The billing tables were tangled in ways the design doc never mentioned, and Q2 went almost entirely to untangling them before we moved a single service. Worth it anyway: checkout p95 fell from 900ms to 310ms.

The counts: 1,247 PRs merged. Four incidents at Sev-2 or worse, down from eleven. On-call went from six people to nine, which is the boring explanation for that second number.

What we skipped: feature flag cleanup. There are 340 dead flags in the tree, and I have pushed that ticket back four times myself. The docs rewrite stalled in March. If you were blocked on either, blame me. Both sit on the Q1 list now, each with a name next to it this time.

Two people joined. Welcome, Priya and Sam. One left: Marcus, thank you for seven years.

What I want next year is dull. Fewer fronts open at once. We ran five initiatives in parallel and shipped three. Three, shipped, would have felt better and cost less.

See you Monday.

---
